	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS
	Students will understand that…
•  Numbers can always be composed of 10 ones and some more ones.
•  Shapes can be identified as flat or solid.
•  Concrete, representational, and abstract representations of teen numbers connect to one another.
	Students will keep considering…
•  How do I compose and decompose teen numbers using tens and ones?
•  How can I use flat and solid shapes to draw and build?
•  How do I use drawings and equations to show composing and decomposing teen numbers?

	•  Numbers can always be composed of 10 ones and some more ones
•  How to identify shapes as flat or solid

•  Identifying and naming flat and solid shapes

	SUCCESS CRITERIA
	Learning Target: I know that teen numbers can always be composed of 10 ones and some more ones.
	Success Criterion: I can say that any teen number is made of 10 ones and some extra ones.
	Learning Target: I can identify shapes as flat or solid.
	Success Criterion: I can name examples of flat shapes, name examples of solid shapes, and tell the difference between them.
	Learning Target: I can make connections between concrete, representational, and abstract representations of teen numbers.
	Success Criterion: I can show a teen number with objects, draw a picture of it, write a matching equation, and explain how all three show the same number.
	Learning Target: I can compose and decompose teen numbers using tens and ones.
	Success Criterion: I can put together 10 ones and some more ones to make a teen number, and break apart a teen number into 10 ones and some more ones.
	Learning Target: I can use flat and solid shapes to draw and build.
	Success Criterion: I can choose flat shapes to draw objects and solid shapes to build objects, explaining my choices.
	Learning Target: I can use drawings and equations to show composing and decomposing teen numbers.
	Success Criterion: I can draw a picture and write a matching addition equation for composing and decomposing a teen number.

	Goal: Become a Number and Shape Explorer showing everyone what you know about teen numbers and different kinds of shapes.
Role: You are a Number and Shape Explorer sharing your discoveries with your classmates and teacher.
Audience: Your classmates and your teacher.
